content.text:
I haven't been able to create the three tip products yet; it can't be done from here today. I pushed the setup that creates them automatically on the next Android release, which will be the release that ships this PR. It's commit `4afd3df7` on PR #2578; CI is running on it now.

**Why not now:**
- **No access from here:** your local gcloud login doesn't include access to the Google Play API. Play answered "insufficient authentication scopes". Only the deploy's service account (the `PLAY_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_JSON` GitHub secret) has that access.
- **Play would refuse:** Play only accepts in-app products once a bundle with the billing permission is on a track. The bundle on Play now doesn't have it; this PR adds it.

**What I pushed:**
- `apps/bacteria-wars-android/store/tips.json` lists the products, with German and English titles:

  | Product | Title (EN / DE) | Price in Germany |
  |---|---|---|
  | `tip_small` | Small coffee / Kleiner Kaffee | 2,99 € |
  | `tip_medium` | Large coffee / Großer Kaffee | 4,99 € |
  | `tip_large` | Coffee and cake / Kaffee mit Kuchen | 9,99 € |

  Play converts these prices for every other country.
- `tools/bacteria-game/play-tips.ts` creates or updates the products and activates them, modelled on movepath's `publish-play-tips`. The Android deploy runs it right after uploading the bundle.
- If creating the products fails (for example, no payments profile yet), the deploy finishes the release and store listing first and only then reports the error.
- Broken product texts stop the deploy before the build.

I checked the code against a fake Play API, which made the expected calls, and lint and type checks pass. It hasn't run against the real Play API yet; the first real run is that release.

**Two things only you can do in the Play Console, before that release:**
1. Link a payments profile; without one, Play rejects every in-app product.
2. Give the service account permission to manage in-app products (Users and permissions → the service account → app permissions).

If you'd rather create the products right away, you could log in locally with Play API access: `gcloud auth application-default login --scopes=https://www.googleapis.com/auth/androidpublisher,https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform`. Play would still refuse them until the billing bundle is on a track, though.

content.text:
The tips aren't on Google Play yet. Your login worked and Play accepted the requests, but it refused to create them: *"Can't create product. To fix, request billing permission."* Play only allows in-app products once an app bundle with the billing permission has been uploaded. The bundle on Play now doesn't have it; this PR adds it.

So I squash-merged PR #2578 (as `e71d73c1`). CI was fully green and the PR merged cleanly. The release that merge started is running now (run `40011955223`). It uploads the new billing bundle to the internal track and then creates the three tips: Small coffee 2,99 €, Large coffee 4,99 €, Coffee and cake 9,99 € in Germany. I'm watching the run and will tell you whether the tips were created.

Two things that could still stop the tips in that run, both Play Console settings only you can change:
- **Payments profile:** one must be linked to the Play Console.
- **Service account permission:** the deploy's service account needs permission to manage in-app products.

If the run fails on either, fix it in the Console and I can create the tips right away with your new local login. That also works for any other Play API call. I sent `bacteria-wars` as the billing project with each request, so your gcloud settings are unchanged.

I also stopped watching the merged PR and cancelled the reminder I had scheduled for it.

fix(bacteria-wars-android): 🐛 read the tip products where Play has them

The deploy read an existing tip from `onetimeproducts/<id>`, which Play
answers with a 404 page: every deploy took the tips for new ones and
activated them again. Reads go to `oneTimeProducts/<id>`; writes keep the
lower-case path. Checked against Play: a run now updates the three tips
and leaves their active purchase option alone.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF
gh pr create -R WolfSoko/wol-sok-mono --base main --head feat/bacteria-wars-support --title "fix(bacteria-wars-android): 🐛 read the tip products where Play has them" --body "$(cat <<'EOF'
## Summary

The Android deploy (`tools/bacteria-game/play-tips.ts`, from #2578) read an existing tip from `onetimeproducts/<id>`. Play answers that path with an HTML 404, so every deploy took the tips for new ones and activated their purchase option again. Reads now go to `oneTimeProducts/<id>`; the upsert keeps the lower-case path, which Play accepts.

## Testing

- Ran the publisher against the real Play API: it now reports *Updated* for `tip_small`, `tip_medium`, `tip_large` and skips activation; reading them back shows all three `ACTIVE` at 2,99 / 4,99 / 9,99 € in DE.
- oxlint and `tsc --strict` on the deploy tool are clean.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
EOF
)"

content.text:
The three tips are live on Google Play. The v74.54.0 release uploaded the app with billing turned on, and its deploy then created the products. I read them back from Play:

| Product | Titles (DE / EN) | State | Price in DE |
|---|---|---|---|
| `tip_small` | Kleiner Kaffee / Small coffee | active | 2,99 € |
| `tip_medium` | Großer Kaffee / Large coffee | active | 4,99 € |
| `tip_large` | Kaffee mit Kuchen / Coffee and cake | active | 9,99 € |

The Play app should offer them as soon as players get the v74.54.0 build. For now that build is only on the internal testing track; production comes when you promote it in the Play Console. I haven't tried a purchase on a phone yet.

**Follow-up fix, PR #2582:** while checking the products I found a small bug in my deploy code. It read each product from a URL that Play answers with a 404 page, so every deploy treated the tips as new and switched them on again. It did no harm, but it was wrong. I fixed the URL and re-ran the publisher against the real Play API: it now reports the tips as updated and leaves them alone. CI is running on the PR (https://github.com/WolfSoko/wol-sok-mono/pull/2582). I'm watching it and will squash-merge once it's green.

**Something else failed in the same release:** publishing the npm package `@wolsok/thanos` failed. npm answered "Not found / you do not have permission" on the upload, which usually means the npm token in GitHub has expired or lost access. The pipeline opened issue #2581 for it. I haven't looked into it further; it most likely needs a new npm token in the repo secrets.

content.text:
You don't have the ad unit ID yet; you create an ad unit in AdSense to get one:

1. In adsense.google.com, go to **Ads** → **By ad unit** → **Display ads**.
2. Name it (for example "Bacteria Wars menu"), keep **Responsive**, and click **Create**.
3. AdSense then shows a code snippet. The ad unit ID is the number in it:
   ```html
   data-ad-slot="1234567890"
   ```

Paste that number or the whole snippet here and I'll put it into `environment.prod.ts` as `support.ads`. From then on the game shows ads on *How to play* and *Profile* once the player has answered the consent banner.

While you do that, keep **Auto ads** off for bacteria-wars.wolsok.de (Ads → By site → the site → Auto ads off). Otherwise Google's own banner and full-screen ads would cover the game.

The code you pasted is in PR #2583 (https://github.com/WolfSoko/wol-sok-mono/pull/2583). It goes in the page head of `index.html`, where AdSense looks for it to verify the site, together with the `google-adsense-account` tag. The production build has it exactly once, and the app's unit tests pass. The script also shows Google's consent banner on every visit from now on, even before any ad unit is set. It's only on bacteria-wars.wolsok.de, not on the angular-examples site.

CI is running on #2583. I'll squash-merge it once CI is green. The live game picks the code up with the next release.

- Tips and ads live in the game lib's `support/` folder and are switched on by `provideGameSupport` in the remote's app config only, so the shell shows neither. On the web the game links to Buy Me a Coffee; in the app it sells Play tips instead (Play allows no other donation link). The remote's `index.html` loads the AdSense script (it brings Google's consent banner, and AdSense checks the site by it); the game's own ad slots stay off until `environment.prod.ts` sets `support.ads` (publisher id and ad unit). Keep Auto ads off for the subdomain in AdSense, or ads cover the game. The shared tip settings are in `environments/game-support.ts`. Changes to them belong into the privacy policy (`src/app/privacy`) too.

- `store/` holds what Play shows: the listing texts and graphics, the promo videos and, in `store/play-games/achievements/`, the Play Games Services achievement icons (`npx nx run bacteria-wars-android:achievement-icons`). The achievements themselves are the game's: `play-games-achievements.json` in `libs/features/lazy/bacteria-game/src/lib/state/`, with its spec keeping it in line with the game's achievements. PR #2583 has been auto-merged into main, so the AdSense script and the `google-adsense-account` tag are on main. The next release deploys them to bacteria-wars.wolsok.de, and AdSense can verify the site from then on. I've stopped watching the PR and cancelled the reminder.

Two things are left for you in AdSense:
- **Ad unit ID:** create a display ad unit (Ads → By ad unit → Display ads) and send me the number from `data-ad-slot="…"`. I'll put it into `environment.prod.ts`, which turns on the ads on the *How to play* and *Profile* screens.
- **Auto ads:** turn Auto ads off for bacteria-wars.wolsok.de. Otherwise Google's banner and full-screen ads would cover the game.
